basis: docs/measurement-basis.md#authorization-coverage, published 2026-11-09; definition unchanged for this reading
method: Census, not a sample. Every externally consequential action class named in the definition is enumerated exactly once and scored against files in the reviewed commit plus one live reading of repository settings. A class is covered only when the tree names both (a) the person or role who decides and (b) the place the decision is written down. A mechanical gate, a prohibition, a limit or a CI check is a control, not an authorizer; a validator output is evidence, not a decision record.
denominator_basis: The definition names six groups. Three are split because their alternatives have different external effects and different possible deciders or records: release vs leaderboard publication, issue comment vs issue close, and the governance document vs repository settings. The other three (spending money, using a credential, stating an external conclusion) stay whole. This yields the nine classes below.

branch_protection_reading.note: A live setting, not a tree file. Recorded here because it bears on whether named owners are enforced; enforcement is not part of this metric's numerator.

action_classes.action: Publishing a release (tag, package artifact and changelog entry)
action_classes.external_consequence: A version becomes publicly installable and citable.
action_classes.decision_record: The annotated vX.Y.Z tag with its CHANGELOG.md entry; the canonical gates (dsa verify-release, full pytest, SBOM regeneration) are the stated precondition.
action_classes.reason: Both parts of the numerator are named: who may tag, and where the tag and its changelog entry live.

action_classes.action: Promoting a real-model result to a public leaderboard row or external comparison claim
action_classes.external_consequence: A quantitative quality claim about the system becomes public.
action_classes.reason: The publication rule is a mechanical gate over artifact fields and names no person or role authorized to promote a row. matrix_validation.json records validator output, not a decision to publish.

action_classes.external_consequence: A statement is made in the project's name in a public forum.
existing_controls: GOVERNANCE.md:12 (contributors may take part in issues and discussions)
action_classes.reason: Contributors are named as actors, not as authorizers of a statement made on the project's behalf. The triage SLA is a timing rule, and no location is named where the decision to comment is recorded.

action_classes.external_consequence: An externally visible request or report changes state, possibly without a fix.
existing_controls: GOVERNANCE.md:11 (final say on merges, releases, security response, roadmap)
GOVERNANCE.md:30-31 (triage SLA and no fix-commitment SLA)
action_classes.reason: The maintainer's enumerated powers do not include closing a public issue, and the tree names no place where that decision is recorded.

action_classes.action: Changing the governance document (GOVERNANCE.md) or a comparable policy file
action_classes.external_consequence: The published allocation of authority changes.
action_classes.decision_record: The pull request and its merge commit on main, which is both the review trail and the resulting text.
existing_controls: CODEOWNERS names an owner for every path
action_classes.reason: The decider and the record are both named. Caveat recorded separately: the branch protection reading shows no required review, so the named owner is advisory rather than enforced.

action_classes.action: Changing branch protection or repository settings
action_classes.external_consequence: The set of checks and reviewers standing between a change and main changes.
existing_controls: branch protection: required status check ci, strict=true (live reading in this record)
action_classes.reason: A settings change is not a merge, so the ci requirement does not govern it. No tree file names who may change settings or where that decision is written down; the settings value itself was read from the API for this record.

action_classes.action: Spending money or enabling a credentialed paid model lane
action_classes.external_consequence: A billable action is taken against the zero-billing constraint.
existing_controls: docs/real-model-evaluation.md:137-142 (DSA_MAX_COST_USD per-process cap and project-level limit)
action_classes.reason: A prohibition and a per-process cap are limits, not an authorizer. ADR-003 names an opt-in exception for explicitly enabled model tokens but does not name who grants it or where the grant is recorded.

action_classes.action: Adding, rotating or using a repository credential
action_classes.external_consequence: An external service is accessed with the project's identity.
existing_controls: GOVERNANCE.md:35-36 (keys stay in the user's environment)
action_classes.reason: The workflow consumes repository secrets and SECURITY.md forbids committing them, but no file names who may add, rotate or authorize their use and there is no credential-use record. Secret scanning detects a leaked value; it does not record a decision.

action_classes.action: Stating an external conclusion outside a leaderboard row (capability, security, currency or compatibility claims)
action_classes.external_consequence: A claim about the product is published to users or reviewers.
action_classes.reason: The guard tests reject some classes of unsupported claim mechanically. They name no authorizer and no record of who decided a conclusion was sound; a green guard shows consistency, not authorization.

scope_note: This reading measures only whether the tree names a decider and a record. It does not measure whether any decision was correct, whether it was enforced, or whether an external action occurred. ADR-003's INV6 row rates the actions taken by that ADR (none), not global coverage, so a low reading here is not a contradiction of it.
proposed_amendment: NOT APPLIED. A single decision-authority table in GOVERNANCE.md with columns (action class, authorizer, where the decision is recorded, whether review is required) would close the seven gaps: name the maintainer for AC2/AC3/AC4/AC6/AC7/AC8/AC9, name the PR/matrix artifact/credential ledger/settings baseline as each record, and state that a named authorizer is required before the corresponding external action. Changing GOVERNANCE.md is itself a governed action, so this proposal needs its own decision before a second reading is taken under the same basis. The first reading stays as recorded here.
